title: Water: The Essence of Life
seo_title: Water Class 5 EVS Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 1)
standard_code: Class 5, Our Wondrous World Chapter 1: Water
standard_text: Forms of water (solid, liquid and gas) and how water changes form; sources of water such as rain, rivers, glaciers, lakes and groundwater; how flowing water shapes the land; life in fresh water; why water is precious and ways to save it (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 1).

key_big: No living thing can live without water.
key_sub: Only a little of Earth's water is fresh.
body_html:
How to think about it

About three-fourths of Earth is covered with water, but most is salty sea water; fresh water is stored in glaciers, rivers, lakes and under the ground. Water exists as solid ice, liquid water and invisible water vapour. Heating makes it evaporate, cooling makes vapour condense into drops and freezing turns it into ice.

Flowing water cuts valleys and carries soil. Fish, frogs, lotuses and ducks are adapted to life in fresh water. Because fresh water is limited, we save it: fix leaks, use buckets instead of showers, harvest rainwater and keep ponds clean.

Example

Drops on a cold glass come from…

vapour in the air cools

Answer: condensation

Example

A tap wastes 8 L a day. In 7 days?

8 × 7

Answer: 56 litres

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water vapour is the white steam you can see.
  • Thinking most of Earth's water can be drunk.
  • Thinking groundwater never runs out.
